claims.claim_text: The indexed Edward V. Baranski is the University of Illinois alumnus and Army captain documented in official histories of the OSS mission to Czechoslovakia.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Captain Baranski served with the 2677th Regiment, Office of Strategic Services, U.S. Army.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The institutional profile and two federal histories independently converge on Baranski's full name or middle initial, captain rank, Army service, 2677th Regiment, OSS assignment, and Czechoslovakia mission.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence based on the uncommon full name, matching middle initial, captain rank, Army and OSS service, 2677th Regiment, Illinois connection, and mutually consistent institutional and federal sources.
claims.temporal_assessment: The sources place this identity in the Army and OSS during 1944; the University of Illinois profile dates his graduation to 1941.
claims.match_notes: The physical Box 35 file has not been inspected. The corroboration is substantially stronger than a name match, but the project therefore retains high-confidence rather than confirmed status.

claims.evidence_paraphrase: The University of Illinois Alumni Association account explicitly places Baranski as an Army mess sergeant when he volunteered and says the OSS then accepted him.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence identity based on the uncommon full name and corroborating rank, branch, OSS unit, mission, and Illinois details across institutional and federal sources.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicit immediate sequence: Army mess-sergeant service at the time of volunteering, followed by OSS acceptance and promotion in 1944.
claims.match_notes: Model as a military assignment, not civilian employment. No narrower Army unit or exact transfer date is inferred.
